newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-RENE LACOSTE, LAST OF TENNIS MUSKETEERS, DIES AT 92.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RENE LACOSTE, LAST OF TENNIS MUSKETEERS, DIES AT 92.

text.p: Rene Lacoste, the last survivor of the four French "musketeers" who dominated the tennis world in the late 1920s and won the Davis Cup for France every year from 1927 to 1932, has died aged 92, his family said on Sunday.
Lacoste, nicknamed "The Crocodile" as a player, was also the designer of a polo shirt which carried his name and was recognised around the world by its trademark crocodile over the left breast.
He died on Saturday at his home in St. Jean-de-Luz, southwest France, his family said.
Lacoste and fellow musketeers Henri Cochet, Jean Borotra and Jacques Brugnon swept the Wimbledon singles title six times in succession from 1924 to 1929.
He personally won the title in 1925 and 1928 and also took the U.S. Open in 1926 and 1927 when ranked world number one. Lacoste also won the French Open three times, in 1925, 1927 and 1929.
Lacoste quit tennis early, at the age of 25, to go into business and became managing director of several firms including Air-Equipment and Bendix-Lockheed-Air Equipment.
He was married to Simone Thion la Chaume, a former golf champion.
